newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq to pay interim div as FID.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq to pay interim div as FID.

text.p: British drinks group Allied Domecq Plc said on Wednesday that it has decided to pay its interim dividend as a foreign income dividend (FID).

The company said that the FID would be paid at the net level of 9.44p per share and that the move would enable Allied to obtain a refund of 25 million stg advanced corporation tax (ACT) paid on the FID.
Allied Domecq had announced on May 13 that it would be paying an interim dividend of 9.44p per share to shareholders on July 25.

However, as a result of paying the FID, those shareholders who had originally elected to receive a scrip dividend instead of a cash dividend will now receive a cash dividend payment of 9.44p per share.
In recent years, the drinks firm had paid 72 million stg of ACT which it was unable to offset against corporation tax.
The company's decision to pay an FID follows UK government changes to the regime relating to the taxation of dividends at its budget on July 2.
